sections.old: nay, that they did not wish to punish it with a simple banishment, unless when the adultery was joined with incest
sections.new: nay, that they wished to punish it only with a simple banishment, unless when the adultery was joined with incest
sections.reason: Fidelity: *voire que ne l'ayent voulu punir d'vn ſimple banniſſement* intensifies "not capital" — the ordinary Roman penalty was relegation, capital only where incest was joined (note d); the English inverted it so that incest earned mere banishment.

sections.new: And other offences,
sections.reason: Consistency: the word of the decision, rendered "other offences" at texte-80 (decision cas → offences).

sections.new: The other offences are several other acts of cheating
sections.reason: Consistency: expounds the decision's *autres cas* → "other offences" (texte-80, texte-89).

findings.note: [unclear] left on *ſemblẽt peu, ou point meriter quelque excuſe*: the opinion Coras reports (and then rejects as impious) needs "seem to deserve some excuse"; the whole book offers no parallel to fix the dropped word. Possibly *peine* fell out before *quelque excuſe* ("little or no penalty, [but] some excuse").
The heading of the next annotation (annot-084) is printed ANNOT. LXXXIII. for LXXXIV; the French keeps it, our numbering follows the true count.
[unclear] left: *faiſant le premier miracle, diſant à ſes Apoſtres {a2}* breaks off; note a2 is John 2 (Cana), and no words of Christ follow. Nothing in the book supplies them.

*les parens des meurtris, offenſez, reçoyuent quelque allegement* is rendered "the kinsfolk of the murdered and the injured may receive". Callistratus (D. 48.19.28.15: *solacio sit cognatis et adfinibus interemptorum*) suggests *offenſez* qualifies the kinsfolk ("the kinsfolk of the murdered, [thus] wronged") rather than adding a class; the French comma allows either. Left for the reviewer.

The print's Virgil reads *Et nondum informis lethi*; the English parenthesis gives the correct *nodum* (Aen. 12.603) silently, as the translators normalised Latin quotations elsewhere. A compositor's error, not a transcription doubt.
*Les meſchans auſſi ne euident pas moins* — *euident* is *cuident* (believe), so translated; logged in the misreadings file.
Note p (*P. interdũ: et illec Accurſe*) has no marker in the body; not a translation matter.
The 1555 [unclear] on Saint-Quentin stands per pass-0; the battle was 10 August 1557.

*l'inſtabilité auſſi, diſcretion, & temerité, eſt peculiere à la ieuneſſe*: the print's *diſcretion* is rendered "indiscretion", the only sense the list allows (cf. *indiſcretement* earlier in the same annotation).
*d'auoir participé auec ſes fils* (p141) is translated "daughters", which the story requires; logged in the misreadings file.
Davis's reading rests on this annotation and annot-097 (case file §10); both were checked sentence by sentence and found faithful, hesitations and all. Nothing was smoothed.
*ceux qui ſuruiennent à l'execution de la peine* is translated "survive"; the print's *ſuruiennent* is probably *ſuruiuent*; logged in the misreadings file.

[unclear] on *telles defenſes ſont priuées* left. The maxim *privatorum conventio iuri publico non derogat* and the following clause (*ne peuuent empeſcher la force des loix equitables*) support "private" as printed — a private man's prohibition cannot bar the bishop's legal duty — so the next pass may fairly remove the flag; *praves* remains possible.
Note q (*P. ſi quis igitur non implens*) has no marker in the body; not a translation matter.
Ringold–Lewis: "robbery" for *Larrecin*; ours "Theft" per §9. Interpretive; ours matches texte-80 and annot-087.
Ringold–Lewis: "other such offenses" for *autres cas*; supports the decision cas → offences.
Ringold–Lewis: "excluded and excludes from the case" for *met hors de procez, & d'inſtance*; ours "dismisses from the case and suit" per §5. Same meaning.
Ringold–Lewis: "has dismissed and sends this to the said judge" for *a renuoyé, & renuoye*; ours "has remanded, and remands". Theirs loses the technical sense of remanding for execution; ours right.
Ringold–Lewis agree in substance ("confessed at great length his impudent and daring misdeed").

Ringold–Lewis: "Pierre de Guilhet, inhabitant of Mane" for *hoſte du lieu de Mane*; *hoſte* is innkeeper (as at texte-32, *hoſte de Touges*), and our print reads *Guilher* (§3). Ours right on both; they also drop *maiſtre*.

Ringold–Lewis and we both supply the missing verb (*ce qu'iceluy Martin [ſouloit] dire, & faire*); ours keeps the [unclear] flag. They render *cautement* "as cleverly as possible", we "as warily as he could"; *caut* is cunning/wary, interpretive.
Ringold–Lewis: "a rascal in many ways, even having committed several thefts and outrages"; *affrontemens* is cheating, not outrage. Ours right.

Ringold–Lewis: "whom in this way he had already placed in authority" for *lequel au moyen de ce, il a ia mis en inſtance*; *mettre en inſtance* is to sue (texte-14, texte-18). Ours right. Their "hundredweights" for *quintaux* is equivalent.
Ringold–Lewis agree ("resident of Pin", "guardians").
Ringold–Lewis: "executors of his will"; ours "testament" per §9 (*testament* throughout annot-110).
The embedded TEXTE (*Depuis pour executer ledict arreſt … ouy par ledit Iuge de Rieux*) agrees with Ringold–Lewis in substance.
Alts in the body and margin resolved from the book's own usage (p126-b0l8-1, p126-m5l0-1); see the alt-choices file.

Punctuation-only alts in the margins of annot-083, 094, 095, 096, 097, 098, 101, 107, 108, 109 and 110 (a pointed vs unpointed abbreviation, comma vs point) were left unchosen except where the same citation elsewhere in the book gives the form; none affects the English.
